title: J-ART: A Japanese Adversarial Red-Team Framework for Application-Layer LLM Security and Cost-Efficiency
description:
J-ART is an open, reproducible harness that evaluates the application-structure layer of LLM deployments (model x system-prompt strength x guardrail x retrieval), not bare models. It applies Japanese-specific obfuscation transforms (gyaru-moji, vertical/newline splitting, keigo framing, double-talk, Base64, leet/zero-width smuggling) that defeat naive keyword filters, grounds attacks in MITRE ATLAS (10 inference-time techniques), compares five guardrail settings (none / keyword / normalizing-regex / LLM / Llama Guard), and reports a defense rate with Wilson and cluster-robust 95% confidence intervals alongside a cost-efficiency metric. Attacks use harmless proxy markers (a fictitious canary and benign output markers); no weaponizable content is included, and the malicious instruction core is masked in all published result artifacts and on the public site (the cores themselves are in the public source code).

Version 0.2.0 reports a fully-labeled live K=5 campaign over 21 application configurations (8,085 trials), a balanced three-model ablation with cluster-robust bootstrap intervals, committed LIVE result artifacts (experiments/var_run.json and the ablation files) from which every result reproduces, a unit-test-audited core-masking invariant, and an ATLAS-OWASP-NIST-EU-AI-Act-Japan governance crosswalk.

This record archives the code, configuration, the technical report (English and Japanese; included up to v0.2.0, now maintained outside this repository), the committed LIVE result artifacts, and the deployment workflow.

Version 0.4.0 adds nine Japanese script transforms split by whether Unicode NFKC undoes them (half-width kana, combining voiced marks and Kangxi/compatibility ideographs versus kana exchange, kana-kanji look-alikes and simplified/traditional kanji), a staged normalizing filter with a skeleton-matching guardrail, a deterministic transform-by-filter matrix, a hand-written benign request set for false-positive counting, and a LIVE K=3 measurement of the new transforms on three models (experiments/expansion_run.json).
